summary: This bill raises the excise tax on remittance transfers from 1% to 25%, removes prior limitations and exemptions, directs the revenue to deficit reduction, and creates a refundable tax credit for U.S. citizens who pay the tax on transfers made for business or travel purposes.

scores.thoughts: The bill does not alter any government spending programs, appropriations, or outlays. It only modifies tax revenue collection and directs resulting funds to deficit reduction. No provisions expand or contract spending levels.

Section 2 raises the excise tax on remittance transfers from 1% to 25% and removes prior limitations. This constitutes a substantial tax increase, even though a partial credit is later provided for certain U.S. citizen payers. The dominant effect is higher taxation.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, providers, or public health programs.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill dramatically increases the cost of sending remittances abroad, a primary financial activity of many immigrant communities. By design it seeks to reduce external monetary outflows tied to immigration, producing a clear restrictive effect on immigration-related financial flows.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense authorizations, or related spending.
No provisions address environmental regulation, climate policy, or natural resources.
No provisions modify welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
No provisions address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill concerns personal remittance transfers rather than tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.

Subsection 2(e) explicitly requires that all revenue from the increased excise tax be deposited in the general fund 'for the sole purpose of deficit reduction.' This directly prioritizes debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill targets private remittance transfers, not government foreign aid appropriations or programs.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
